title: Introduction
subtitle: What is the Rapture?

pretrib.summary: The rapture is a literal catching away of the church before the final Tribulation.
pretrib.teaching: Pre-tribulation Christians teach that Jesus first comes for His church before the Tribulation. The dead in Christ are resurrected, living believers are instantly transformed, and both groups are caught up to meet Christ in the air. This is distinguished from Christ’s later visible return to earth after the Tribulation.

support.why: Paul explicitly describes the dead in Christ rising and living believers being caught up to meet the Lord in the air.
The sudden transformation of living believers and resurrection of the dead is connected with the rapture.
Jesus’ promise to come again and receive His followers is understood as taking the church to the Father’s house.

adventist.summary: The catching up is real, but it occurs at Christ’s one visible and glorious Second Coming.
adventist.teaching: Seventh-day Adventists also affirm the resurrection of the righteous and the catching up of living believers. They understand these events as part of one visible, audible Second Coming at the end of the age, not as a secret event separated from the final coming by several years.

support.why: The passage combines Christ’s descent, a shout, the archangel’s voice, trumpet, resurrection, and catching up in one sequence.
Christ’s return is described as visible to every eye.
The Son of Man appears visibly and gathers His elect with a great trumpet.

bible_first: The Bible clearly teaches a real catching up of believers. The central debate is whether this catching up is a separate pre-Tribulation event or part of the visible Second Coming.
takeaways: The rapture itself is explicitly biblical.
The dead in Christ rise first.
Living believers are transformed and caught up.
The major disagreement concerns timing and whether Christ’s return occurs in one stage or two.

title: Key Questions
subtitle: Main topics to explore

pretrib.summary: Pre-tribulation theology answers the major questions by separating the rapture from Christ’s later visible return.
pretrib.teaching: The pre-tribulation system distinguishes Christ coming for His church from Christ later coming with His saints. This distinction is used to explain why some passages describe believers meeting Christ in the air while others describe Him returning visibly in judgment.

support.why: Used as the primary passage for Christ coming for the church.
Often understood as Christ’s later visible post-Tribulation return.

adventist.summary: Adventists understand the major rapture passages as complementary descriptions of one final return.
adventist.teaching: Adventists compare the trumpet, resurrection, visible appearing, gathering of the elect, and destruction of evil and understand these as features of the same Second Coming.

support.why: The visible appearing, trumpet, and gathering are presented together.
The resurrection and catching up occur when Christ descends from heaven.
Christ’s coming and our gathering to Him are discussed together.

bible_first: The best way to evaluate the two views is to identify which conclusions are explicitly stated by the passages and which depend on linking or separating passages through a theological framework.
takeaways: Is the rapture secret or public?
Does it occur before or after the Tribulation?
Are Matthew 24 and 1 Thessalonians 4 the same event?
Does Scripture explicitly teach two stages of Christ’s return?

title: Is the Rapture Secret?
subtitle: Is Christ’s coming invisible or public?

pretrib.summary: Pre-trib believers emphasize a sudden, unexpected removal of the church before the Tribulation.
pretrib.teaching: Many pre-tribulation Christians use the expression 'secret rapture' to describe the church being suddenly taken before the Tribulation. The emphasis is often on surprise and the world not being prepared. Some pre-trib teachers do not claim that the event itself is literally silent; rather, they distinguish it from the later universally visible return.

support.why: The coming day is compared with a thief in the night, emphasizing unexpectedness.
The unknown hour and one-taken/one-left language are interpreted as sudden separation.
Christ’s receiving of believers is interpreted as occurring before His later public return.

adventist.summary: Adventists reject a secret Second Coming and teach that Christ’s return is visible, audible, and unmistakable.
adventist.teaching: Adventists point to the shout, archangel’s voice, trumpet of God, resurrection of the dead, lightning-like visibility of Christ’s coming, and the statement that every eye will see Him. These features are viewed as incompatible with an invisible final return.

support.why: The passage explicitly describes a shout, archangel’s voice, trumpet, resurrection, and gathering.
Every eye sees Christ.
Christ compares His coming to lightning visible across the sky.
The nations see the Son of Man coming in power and great glory.

bible_first: Scripture clearly teaches that Christ’s return is sudden and unexpected for the unprepared. But the main rapture passage itself contains public, audible elements. 'Unexpected' is not automatically the same as 'invisible.'
takeaways: The word 'secret' does not appear in 1 Thessalonians 4.
A shout, archangel’s voice, and trumpet are explicitly mentioned.
Revelation says every eye will see Christ.
The key issue is whether the rapture is a separate earlier event from the visible return.

title: When Does It Happen?
subtitle: Before, during, or after the Tribulation?

pretrib.summary: The church is raptured before the Tribulation begins.
pretrib.teaching: Pre-tribulation Christians usually understand the final Tribulation as a distinct period of divine judgment. Because the church is not appointed to wrath and because Revelation promises protection from the coming hour of testing, they conclude that the church is removed before that period begins.

support.why: Believers are not appointed to wrath.
Being kept 'from the hour of temptation' is interpreted as removal before the worldwide testing.
Some interpret the promise to escape coming events as supporting removal before the crisis.

adventist.summary: God’s people pass through the final crisis but are preserved and gathered when Christ returns.
adventist.teaching: Adventists distinguish persecution and tribulation from God’s final wrath. They understand the final generation of believers as present during the end-time crisis, protected by God, and delivered at Christ’s visible return.

support.why: Jesus places the visible coming and gathering of the elect after the tribulation.
God’s people are present during the time of trouble and are delivered.
The saints are pictured as enduring faithfully during the final conflict.

bible_first: Matthew 24 gives a direct sequence: tribulation, cosmic signs, visible coming of the Son of Man, trumpet, and gathering of the elect. Pre-tribulation theology therefore must understand this gathering as different from the earlier church rapture.
takeaways: Pre-tribulation theology places the rapture before the final Tribulation.
Matthew 24 places a gathering of the elect after tribulation.
'Not appointed to wrath' does not by itself specify physical removal from earth.
Daniel 12 presents God’s people as delivered in connection with the time of trouble.

title: Who Is Included?
subtitle: Church, elect, righteous, Israel?

pretrib.summary: The rapture specifically concerns the church—dead and living believers in Christ.
pretrib.teaching: Dispensational pre-tribulation theology commonly distinguishes the church from Israel. The church is raptured before the Tribulation, while Israel and people who come to faith during the Tribulation have a different role in the prophetic timeline.

support.why: Paul explicitly refers to 'the dead in Christ' and living believers.
Believers are transformed at the resurrection event.

adventist.summary: All of God’s righteous people are gathered at Christ’s visible return.
adventist.teaching: Adventists do not divide the redeemed into separate prophetic classes that require different future comings. The righteous dead are resurrected, living righteous are transformed, and all are gathered to Christ.

support.why: Christ gathers His elect when He appears.
The righteous dead and living believers are gathered together.
Jesus connects resurrection of believers with the last day.

bible_first: The passages speak of the dead in Christ, living believers, and the elect. Whether these represent separate prophetic groups depends on the larger interpretive framework.
takeaways: The rapture passage explicitly includes dead and living believers in Christ.
Matthew 24 uses the broader term 'elect.'
The major difference is whether the church and Israel require separate prophetic programs.
Both views affirm that believers ultimately belong with Christ.

title: Major Bible Passages
subtitle: Key verses and comparisons

pretrib.summary: The passages are harmonized by assigning them to different stages of Christ’s return.
pretrib.teaching: Pre-tribulation theology typically treats 1 Thessalonians 4 and John 14 as rapture passages while Matthew 24 and Revelation 19 describe the later visible return. The distinction allows the church to be removed before the Tribulation while Christ later returns in judgment.

support.why: Primary rapture passage.
Christ receives believers to Himself.
Usually assigned to the visible post-Tribulation coming.

adventist.summary: The passages are read as complementary descriptions of one final Second Coming.
adventist.teaching: Adventists link the trumpet, resurrection, transformation, gathering, visible appearing, and destruction of evil as elements of one climactic return of Christ.

support.why: The resurrection and transformation occur at the last trumpet.
Christ descends with the trumpet, raises the dead, and gathers believers.
The visible appearing and gathering occur together.
Christ’s coming and our gathering are discussed together.

bible_first: The central interpretive question is whether the passages themselves require two separate comings, or whether they can naturally be read as different descriptions of one event.
takeaways: 1 Thessalonians 4 emphasizes resurrection and catching up.
1 Corinthians 15 emphasizes transformation at the last trumpet.
Matthew 24 emphasizes visible appearing and gathering.
2 Thessalonians 2 links Christ’s coming with our gathering to Him.

title: Differences in Timeline
subtitle: Side-by-side sequence

pretrib.summary: Rapture → Seven-year Tribulation → Visible Return → Millennium.
pretrib.teaching: The standard pre-tribulation sequence begins with the rapture of the church. The Tribulation follows, after which Christ returns visibly with His saints and establishes the millennial kingdom.

support.why: Placed at the beginning of the prophetic sequence as the rapture.
Placed after the Tribulation as the visible return.
Used for the millennial kingdom following Christ’s visible return.

adventist.summary: Final crisis → Visible Second Coming → Resurrection/Gathering → Millennium.
adventist.teaching: Adventists understand the end-time crisis as occurring before the Second Coming. At Christ’s visible return, the righteous dead are raised and the living righteous are transformed and gathered. The redeemed then reign with Christ during the millennium.

support.why: The gathering follows the final tribulation.
Resurrection and gathering occur at Christ’s descent.
The saints reign with Christ during the thousand years.

bible_first: Both timelines use many of the same passages. The central difference is whether the rapture is an earlier event separated from the visible return, or whether the catching up occurs at the visible return itself.
takeaways: Pre-tribulation theology has two stages of Christ’s return.
Adventism teaches one climactic visible return.
Both views include resurrection, gathering, judgment, and a millennium.
The timeline difference comes from how the passages are connected.

title: Summary & Conclusion
subtitle: What can we conclude from the study?

pretrib.summary: The church is raptured before the Tribulation, followed later by Christ’s visible return.
pretrib.teaching: The pre-tribulation view is built on distinguishing the church from Israel, distinguishing the rapture from the visible return, and interpreting promises of deliverance from wrath as removal before the Tribulation.

support.why: Primary passage for the rapture.
Believers are not appointed to wrath.
Interpreted as protection by removal from the coming hour.

adventist.summary: The catching up occurs at Christ’s one visible Second Coming after the final crisis.
adventist.teaching: The Adventist view emphasizes one visible, audible return of Christ accompanied by resurrection, transformation, trumpet, gathering of the elect, judgment, and the beginning of the millennium.

support.why: The visible return and gathering occur after tribulation.
Resurrection and catching up happen when Christ descends.
Every eye sees Christ.

bible_first: The Bible clearly teaches a future catching up of believers. The strongest explicit passages connect that event with Christ’s descent, trumpet, resurrection, transformation, and gathering. A separate secret pre-Tribulation rapture requires additional distinctions between passages and prophetic groups.
takeaways: The rapture itself is clearly biblical.
The timing of the rapture is the central disagreement.
Matthew 24:29-31 is especially important because it explicitly places a gathering after tribulation.
The reader should compare the passages directly and distinguish explicit statements from theological inference.
